variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A communication pattern defines how software components exchange requests, messages, and events. It answers four questions before a protocol or product is chosen:
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Request-response
pairs.detail: Use when the caller needs an immediate result.
pairs.explanation: Use when the caller needs an immediate result. The contract is direct, but downstream latency and failure become part of the caller's path.

pairs.label: Work queue
pairs.detail: Use when work can finish later.
pairs.explanation: Use when work can finish later. The queue absorbs bursts and lets workers scale independently, but handlers must tolerate retries.

pairs.label: Event stream
pairs.detail: Use when several capabilities react to a fact that already happened.
pairs.explanation: Use when several capabilities react to a fact that already happened. Replay and fan-out improve flexibility while making ordering and schema evolution explicit.

variants.hint:
Request-response: Use when the caller needs an immediate result.

Work queue: Use when work can finish later.

Event stream: Use when several capabilities react to a fact that already happened.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Validate the order
pairs.detail: Check price, inventory policy, and identity while the user is waiting.
pairs.explanation: Check price, inventory policy, and identity while the user is waiting. Return a clear success or rejection.

pairs.label: Commit intent and outbox
pairs.detail: Store the order and an outgoing event record in one database transaction so state and communication cannot diverge.
pairs.explanation: Store the order and an outgoing event record in one database transaction so state and communication cannot diverge.

pairs.label: Process durable work
pairs.detail: Run payment capture, fulfillment, and email with bounded retries, idempotency keys, and dead-letter handling.
pairs.explanation: Run payment capture, fulfillment, and email with bounded retries, idempotency keys, and dead-letter handling.

pairs.label: Publish business facts
pairs.detail: Let analytics, recommendations, and audit consumers react independently without joining the checkout latency budget.
pairs.explanation: Let analytics, recommendations, and audit consumers react independently without joining the checkout latency budget.

Process durable work: Run payment capture, fulfillment, and email with bounded retries, idempotency keys, and dead-letter handling.

Publish business facts: Let analytics, recommendations, and audit consumers react independently without joining the checkout latency budget.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A communication pattern defines how software components exchange requests, messages, and events. It answers four questions before a protocol or product is chosen:
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Point-to-point queue
pairs.detail: Each work item is handled by one available consumer.
pairs.explanation: Each work item is handled by one available consumer. Use it for image processing, email delivery, and other jobs where workers can share a backlog.

pairs.label: Publish-subscribe
pairs.detail: Each subscriber receives the event through its own subscription.
pairs.explanation: Each subscriber receives the event through its own subscription. Use it when several domains react to the same business fact.

pairs.label: Request-reply with correlation
pairs.detail: A request and later response share a correlation ID.
pairs.explanation: A request and later response share a correlation ID. Use it for long-running work when the caller cannot keep a connection open.

pairs.label: Saga
pairs.detail: Local transactions advance a workflow; compensating actions address partial failure.
pairs.explanation: Local transactions advance a workflow; compensating actions address partial failure. Use it when one database transaction cannot span every service.

variants.hint:
Point-to-point queue: Each work item is handled by one available consumer.

Publish-subscribe: Each subscriber receives the event through its own subscription.

Request-reply with correlation: A request and later response share a correlation ID.

Saga: Local transactions advance a workflow; compensating actions address partial failure.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A communication pattern defines how software components exchange requests, messages, and events. It answers four questions before a protocol or product is chosen:
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Attempt
pairs.detail: Validate the message, check its idempotency key, and perform the smallest durable unit of work.
pairs.explanation: Validate the message, check its idempotency key, and perform the smallest durable unit of work.

pairs.label: Back off
pairs.detail: Retry only errors that can plausibly recover.
pairs.explanation: Retry only errors that can plausibly recover. Add jitter and cap both the delay and total attempts.

pairs.label: Quarantine
pairs.detail: Move exhausted messages to a dead-letter queue with the payload, error, attempt count, and correlation context.
pairs.explanation: Move exhausted messages to a dead-letter queue with the payload, error, attempt count, and correlation context.

pairs.label: Recover
pairs.detail: Fix the cause, replay deliberately, and verify that idempotency protects already completed effects.
pairs.explanation: Fix the cause, replay deliberately, and verify that idempotency protects already completed effects.

variants.hint:
Attempt: Validate the message, check its idempotency key, and perform the smallest durable unit of work.

Back off: Retry only errors that can plausibly recover.

Quarantine: Move exhausted messages to a dead-letter queue with the payload, error, attempt count, and correlation context.

Recover: Fix the cause, replay deliberately, and verify that idempotency protects already completed effects.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: A communication pattern defines how software components exchange requests, messages, and events. It answers four questions before a protocol or product is chosen:
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: HTTP or gRPC
pairs.detail: Good for user-facing commands, service queries, and low-latency internal calls.
pairs.explanation: Good for user-facing commands, service queries, and low-latency internal calls. Protect every dependency with deadlines and cancellation.

pairs.label: RabbitMQ or SQS
pairs.detail: Good for task queues, delayed processing, and competing consumers.
pairs.explanation: Good for task queues, delayed processing, and competing consumers. Define acknowledgment, retry, and dead-letter behavior explicitly.

pairs.label: Kafka or Pulsar
pairs.detail: Good for replayable event streams, high-throughput pipelines, and multiple consumer groups.
pairs.explanation: Good for replayable event streams, high-throughput pipelines, and multiple consumer groups. Partitioning defines ordering and parallelism.

variants.hint:
HTTP or gRPC: Good for user-facing commands, service queries, and low-latency internal calls.

RabbitMQ or SQS: Good for task queues, delayed processing, and competing consumers.

Kafka or Pulsar: Good for replayable event streams, high-throughput pipelines, and multiple consumer groups.
